messages.content: I'll research this on English Wikipedia. Since the session prompt references "the phenomenon and the two candidate explanations" without further specification, I'll work with the canonical case that matches this structure exactly — the **Mandela Effect** (a phenomenon of shared false memories), whose two competing candidate explanations are **(1) memory-based (false memory/confabulation)** and **(2) multiverse/parallel realities**. I'll delegate parallel searches against English Wikipedia to retrieve exact titles and URLs.

subtopics: On English Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org), locate the article(s) covering the 'Mandela effect' phenomenon — the widely reported situation where large groups of people share the same false memory (e.g., misremembering Nelson Mandela dying in prison in the 1980s). Identify which article the page 'Mandela effect' redirects to, and give the exact page title(s), canonical URL(s) (full https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/... form), and a one-sentence description of what each page says about the phenomenon.

On English Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org), find the main articles documenting the psychological/false-memory explanation for shared false memories: 'False memory', 'Confabulation', 'Misinformation effect', 'Source-monitoring error', 'Cryptomnesia', 'Memory conformity'. For each, give the exact page title, canonical URL (full https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/... form), and one sentence on how it explains why groups of people form identical false memories.

On English Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org), find the main articles describing the multiverse / parallel-worlds idea that is popularly invoked to 'explain' the Mandela effect: 'Multiverse', 'Many-worlds interpretation', 'Parallel universes in fiction', and any closely related pages. Give exact page titles, canonical URLs (full https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/... form), and one sentence each on what the article covers and whether it mentions the Mandela effect at all.

On English Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org), find contextual articles relevant to the origin and framing of the term 'Mandela effect': the 'Nelson Mandela' biography (his actual death date in 2013), 'Collective memory', 'Social contagion', and any list-style article covering common misconceptions or popular misrememberings. Return exact page titles, canonical URLs (full https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/... form), and one-sentence relevance notes.
